This is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with Crime No.810/2022 registered at Police Station Rehli, Sagar, District Sagar (M.P.)
for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 366(A), 376, 376(3), 376(2)(N) of IPC and Sections 3/4, 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicants is in custody since 17/09/2022.

Earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 23.11.2022 passed in M.Cr.C.
No.54268 of 2022 granting a liberty to revive the application after recording the statement of the posecutrix.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel for the applicant has filed the order sheets of the trial Court showing that despite making repeated efforts and issuing summon to the prosecutrix, she is not turning to the Court for getting her statement recorded.
However, Shri Malvi, Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State submits that the period of custody and endeavor made by the Court is not enough and sufficient to consider the bail application.
He submits that the trial Court can be directed to adopt the coercive method for calling the prosecutrix and even though if she does not come then this application can be considered.

Considering the aforesaid, this application is disposed of directing trial Court to adopt the coercive method for securing the presence of the prosecutrix or direct the Superintendent of Police of respective area where prosecutrix resides to produce her before the Court so that her statement could be recorded as expeditiously as possible.
With the aforesaid, application is disposed of.

However, liberty is granted to the applicant to revive the application if prosecution failed to produce the prosecutrix before the Court.
Let a copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for necessary compliance.
(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE VPA Manak Lal Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92258710/
